clue.text: A job More devised for a mighty valorous man

indicators.note: devised means worked out or contrived, so the letters of the three words are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Thomas More is credited with inventing a task for a brave warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges A, JOB and MORE. The capital on More is there to suggest Sir Thomas More; it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible (1 Kings 11:28) the king of Israel of this name is called 'a mighty man of valour'.

clue.text: Scholarly cockney, he — and discourteous about it

parts.note: a cockney drops the H, saying 'he' as 'e

indicators.note: about means around, so the rude word goes around it

parts.note: discourteous means rude

explanation.surface: A Londoner is learned, and impolite about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their Hs, so 'he' becomes 'E. 'and' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone erudite is learned and well read, as a scholar is.

clue.text: Charge made by cricket side? Funny thing, in a way

parts.note: on is the leg side of the field in cricket

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the funny thing goes inside the way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a laugh is something funny, as in 'what a laugh'

explanation.surface: An attack by a cricket team, and an amusing thing on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the leg side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs. 'Funny thing' looks like an aside about the charge but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce attacking rush is an onslaught, a charge in the military sense.

clue.text: Mineral aggregate almost vanished in America

parts.note: ore is rock containing a mineral aggregate worth mining

indicators.note: almost says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: vanished means gone

explanation.surface: A mineral deposit has nearly disappeared in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from GONE. The definition is a place in America, a state.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific north-west state is one of the fifty states of the USA, so is found in America.

clue.text: Treat that's 23, it turns out, for an unpopular queen

indicators.note: turns out means comes out altered, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: that's is that is, abbreviated IE (id est)
the answer to 23 across is a word meaning call by name

explanation.surface: A dessert named at 23 proves to be fit for a hated monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges TREAT with IE (that is) and NOMINATE, the answer to 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen guillotined in 1793 was widely despised as extravagant, so an unpopular royal consort.

clue.text: Discovered by the Curies, it keeps a girl in drink

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the drink holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A chemist's discovery is pictured as something that holds a young woman inside a glass of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is part of the surface only; the definition is the Curies' discovery, an element.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie and Pierre Curie isolated this radioactive element in 1898, alongside polonium.

clue.text: Check engineers' stock

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a strain is a breed or line of descent, a stock

explanation.surface: An inspection of the army engineers' supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it.

clue.text: Solicited, so got summoned

definitions.meaning: got summoned means was called to come, asked to attend

explanation.surface: Someone requested, and so was called.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest asked to come has been requested and called to attend, both senses of being asked.

clue.text: County for women, according to Sydney Smith?

definitions.meaning: a former English county around London

definitions.text: for women, according to Sydney Smith?
definitions.meaning: the wit Sydney Smith said there were three sexes, men, women and clergymen, putting women in the middle

explanation.surface: A home county named after something a Regency wit said about women.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Smith, a 19th-century clergyman and wit, joked about 'men, women and clergymen', so women sit between the two; the county was the historic one west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic county west of London shares its name with the 'middle' of three sexes in Smith's joke.

clue.text: Let out about Uncle Sam's struggle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
out means put out of order, so the three letters of Let are rearranged

parts.note: Uncle Sam stands for the USA, so his possessive is US'S, giving USS

explanation.surface: Someone releases something concerning America's struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the three letters of Let into TLE; Uncle Sam's apostrophe-S counts as a letter here, giving USS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a scuffle or hard contest, the same as a struggle.

clue.text: Booked for being uncommunicative

definitions.meaning: booked means kept in advance for someone
uncommunicative means reticent, keeping one's thoughts to oneself

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person is booked in somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A table can be held in advance (booked), and a quiet, aloof person is described with the same word.

clue.text: Washable covering noted at Portsmouth?

definitions.meaning: an apron-like garment worn over clothes to keep them clean
noted means set to music: the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta HMS of this name is set aboard a ship at Portsmouth

explanation.surface: A launderable cover that is famous in a naval port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like 'well known' but means 'set to musical notes': Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera takes place on a warship moored off Portsmouth, a naval city on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a protective apron worn over a dress, and the operetta HMS of that name is set in Portsmouth harbour.

clue.text: Income from religious books — in old Spanish coin

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the books sit within the coin

parts.note: the real was a silver coin of old Spain
NT is the New Testament, the Christian books

explanation.surface: A church earns money from its religious publications, paid in antique Spanish money.
explanation.walkthrough: The real was a silver coin of old Spain; NT for New Testament is a standard abbreviation for religious books.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received from letting property out is rental, a form of income.

clue.text: It's said to be precipitate as a rule

indicators.note: It's said marks that the word is heard spoken, so a soundalike gives the entry

parts.note: to precipitate in weather terms is to fall as water from cloud, to rain

explanation.surface: A claim that it usually pours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' makes RAIN, what precipitation does, sound like the entry. 'as a rule' looks like a phrase meaning 'usually', but 'rule' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty is their reign, the time they hold the rule.

clue.text: Assembly is quieter — it has to be

indicators.note: assembly means putting together, so the letters of the two words are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A gathering is quieter, as it must be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' looks like a noun for a meeting but rearranges IS and QUIETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed or essential is requisite, a thing that must be.

clue.text: Paid with notes for a change? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they were paid in banknotes for variety, and is told the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges PAID and NOTES. 'Quite the opposite' reads as a retort but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Places diametrically across the globe from each other, especially Australia and New Zealand seen from Britain, are opposites.

clue.text: Objectionable description, of 3

definitions.meaning: 3 down is a charge or attack

explanation.surface: An unpleasant way to describe an earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is an attack or charge, which is a military assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant or insulting is offensive, and a large-scale attack is also called by this word.

clue.text: Images abide, including a variety of high-class art

indicators.note: including means containing, so the stay word holds the jumbled piece

parts.note: to abide is to stay

indicators.note: a variety of means a different form of, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is upper-class in the British convention, high-class

explanation.surface: Pictures endure, featuring a range of upmarket art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges U and the word art into TUAR. U meaning upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is sculpture collectively, carved likenesses or images.

clue.text: eg 24. as an estimate of 21

definitions.meaning: the clue at 24 across is a line taken from Shakespeare, an example of a cited passage
21 down is the full value or sum; a builder's price estimate of the sum is called by this name

explanation.surface: Two cross-references: one to a famous line, one to a price.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves point to other clues: 24 across is a line of Shakespeare, and a tradesman's quoted price estimates an amount (21 down).
explanation.definitionFit: Lines repeated from a play are a citation, and a trader's price estimate for a job is also given this name.

clue.text: Noise encountered in spoken services from this book?

indicators.note: encountered in means found inside, so the noise sits within the spoken word

parts.note: oral means spoken
din means noise

explanation.surface: A racket is heard during church services read aloud from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: An ordinal is a little-known word for the book of ordination services, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal is a church service book, setting out the rites of ordination, so services come from it.

clue.text: A fine dilemma created by this appendage!

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a fix is a predicament or dilemma

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a small attachment has caused a real predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: F for fine is a standard abbreviation (pencil grades, and 'fine' in music and stamps).
explanation.definitionFit: Something attached or added on, such as a prefix or suffix, is an appendage.

clue.text: Admit losing Mozart's first anthem

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: intromit is an old word meaning to admit or let in

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Someone concedes losing a Mozart anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: INTROMIT is a rare verb meaning to let in; 'losing' drops M, the first letter of Mozart's.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung as the priest approaches the altar.

clue.text: Full value of one like Bucephalus

parts.note: a means one
Bucephalus was the horse of Alexander the Great, a mount

explanation.surface: The total worth of a famous horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucephalus was Alexander the Great's horse, so an example of a mount.
explanation.definitionFit: The total or sum something comes to is its amount.

clue.text: Order some find enterprising

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that a few people consider commands bold.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce an official requisition for goods is called an indent, a kind of order.

clue.text: Call by name, so perhaps captive bird will appear

indicators.note: captive says one piece is held inside another, imprisoned within it

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale, so an example of a note
the mina (mynah) is a talking bird of the starling family

explanation.surface: A caged bird appears when called by its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale (soh), and the mina is a spelling of mynah, the talking bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for an office is to put them forward by name, to call them by name.

clue.text: "Most — of what he's most assure'd" (Meas. for Meas.)

definitions.text: Most — of what he's most assure'd" (Meas. for Meas

parts.words: Most — of what he's most assure'd" (Meas. for Meas
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing word completes Isabella's line about proud man in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure

explanation.walkthrough: The line, from Act 2 Scene 2 of Measure for Measure, describes man 'dressed in a little brief authority' as most unknowing of what he is surest of.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word means lacking knowledge, unaware of the essence he is so sure of.

clue.text: Sounds altogether a coincidence, this

definitions.meaning: voices or instruments sounding together at the same pitch
agreement or coinciding of things, as in acting in concert

explanation.surface: A remark that it is a fluke when sounds happen together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' looks like a homophone signal, but it is part of the first definition: notes sounded at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing the same note together is singing in concert, and the word also means exact agreement or coinciding.

clue.text: Praise for efficient youth leaders keeping university register

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the leading letters enclose the other pieces
leaders of the two words are their opening letters, which head them

parts.note: a log is a register or record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Commendation for capable young chiefs who maintain a college record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes E and Y; 'keeping' puts U and LOG between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech or writing in high commendation, often at a funeral, is a tribute of praise.

clue.text: Impassioned plea to make agreement on nitrogen verbally

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the letters are said out loud to give the entry

parts.note: a treaty is an agreement; N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, and on means the treaty follows it

explanation.surface: An earnest appeal to sign a pact about a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: N said as a letter is 'en', so N plus TREATY spoken sounds like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest or urgent request is an entreaty, a heartfelt plea.
